texts.preamble: Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 April, 2025 Kabc020231362023 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal , At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.5124/2023
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 16-07-2023 at about 12.00 p.m., the petitioner was crossing the Kasavanahalli main road, in order to go to M. Syphony Apartment for house work, with due care and caution, by observing all traffic rules and regulations. At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 70-H-1578 came in rash and negligent manner, with high speed, endangering to human life and dashed against the petitioner. Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, she was working as house worker and she was earning Rs.20,000/- per month. But, due to accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity. The Bellanduru Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10784262/ 2 petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements. 4. The the respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. Likewise, the respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. Further he has contended that, he was traveling to his home from the work situated at Sri Sai Nilaya, Prashanth Layout, Hoodi, K.R. Puram, Bengaluru, on 14-01-2023 in his motorcycle of the make and model TVS N-Torq bearing Reg. No.KA-70-H- 1578, cautiously, by following the traffic rules and regulations, abiding all the safety rules imposed in the Kasavanahalli Main Road, he was holding valid driving licence bearing No.KA7020190007758, valid till 18-07-2039 and valid insurance. The said motorcycle was insured by respondent No.1 company i.e., M/s. Liberty General Insurance Company Limited. He was riding his motorcycle by following the traffic rules and regulations and tried his best to avoid the impact and also stopped the vehicle immediately to avoid the accident. Despite his due effort, he failed to resist the incident and due to negligence of the petitioner the accident was inevitable. He shifted the petitioner to the Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru and paid the bill of the hospital, with respect to first aid treatment taken by the petitioner.
texts.arguments: It has contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-70-H-1578 and its validity as on the date of accident. It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the motorcycle in the alleged accident. It has contended that, the insured vehicle had no fitness certificate as on the date of alleged accident, the motorcycle in question did not involve in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner. The petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police have created false records and story about the manner and involvement of motorcycle to get compensation and has lodged a false complaint. Further it is contended that, at the time of accident the motorcycle was driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle. The accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was crossing the road without having proper look out at the vehicular movements on the road and without noticing oncoming vehicles and she was crossing the road carelessly and caused the accident. The accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and not due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. Further it is contended that, the petitioner suddenly tried to cross the road from left side, carelessly and without any safety signs, neglecting all the traffic rules and regulations. The petitioner has filed the Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10784262/ 3 present petition with a frivolous intention and to harass this respondent for his no fault. The petitioner was in good health condition on the day itself, the condition of the petitioner was moderate and stable. He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her. For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition. Further it is contended that, the accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was crossing the road carelessly, without having proper look out at the vehicular movements on the road, without noticing oncoming vehicles and resulted in the accident. Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made in her cross-examination that, the accident has taken place due to her own negligence and there was no negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
